sec: Pathogenesis, NBTE, classification, predisposing conditions, organisms, acute IE

items.q: Pathogenesis — match — 1) Mucosal injury 2) Valvular endothelial injury 3) Bacterial seeding … A) Platelet-fibrin clot (NBTE) B) Bacterial adherence to NBTE then proliferation C) Bacteraemia
items.exp: 'Mucosal injury → Bacterial seeding'; 'valvular endothelial injury → Platelet fibrin clot (NBTE) → Bacterial adherence to NBTE → Bacterial proliferation → vegetation → Endocarditic features'. (Book p1048)

items.q: Fill up: 'NBTE — Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis, ______ endocarditis.'
items.exp: 'Note : Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis, marantic endocarditis'. (Book p1048)

items.q: Judge the NBTE note: I NBTE is the non-bacterial thrombotic (marantic) endocarditis. II It is the platelet-fibrin clot on which bacteria later adhere.
items.exp: Both statements reproduce the printed NBTE note and its place in the pathogenetic chain. (Book p1048)

items.q: Which condition is printed alongside NBTE in the note on non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis?
items.exp: 'NBTE in SLE : Catheter / …' is printed next to the marantic-endocarditis note. (Book p1048)

items.q: Classification — match — 1) By valve 2) By exposure … A) Intravenous drug abuse, health-care associated B) Native valve, prosthetic valve
items.exp: 'Infective endocarditis : Native valve, Prosthetic valve, Intravenous drug abuse (IVDA), Health care associated'. (Book p1048)

items.q: In native-valve endocarditis, which valve does the page print as involved?
Native-valve associations — match — 1) Associated valvular heart disease 2) Congenital heart disease 3) CKD-associated IE … A) Ventricular septal defect B) Tricuspid C) MVP with mitral regurgitation
items.exp: 'Associated valvular heart disease : MVP + mitral regurgitation'; 'Congenital heart disease : Ventricular septal defect'; 'CKD associated IE : Tricuspid'. (Book p1048)

items.q: Predisposing conditions in native valves — match — 1) Rheumatic heart disease 2) Congenital heart disease 3) Mitral valve prolapse 4) Degenerative heart disease … A) 10-20% B) Rare C) 10-30% D) 25-30%
items.exp: Printed percentages: rheumatic heart disease 25-30, congenital heart disease 10-20, mitral valve prolapse 10-30, degenerative heart disease Rare. (Book p1048)

items.q: What percentage is printed against parenteral drug abuse in the predisposing-conditions table?
What percentage is printed in the 'None' row of the predisposing-conditions table?

Organisms — match — 1) Native valve 2) Prosthetic valve under 12 months 3) Prosthetic valve over 12 months 4) IV drug use associated … A) CoNS > MRSA > Gram-negative bacilli B) MRSA C) S. aureus > Streptococcus viridans > enterococci D) Streptococcus viridans > S. aureus > enterococci
items.exp: 'Native valve : S. aureus > Streptococcus viridans > enterococci'; 'Prosthetic valve : < 12 months : CoNS > mRSA > Gram -ve bacilli; > 12 months : Streptococcus viridans > S. aureus > enterococci'; 'IV drug users associated IE : mRSA'. (Book p1048)

items.q: Which organism heads the list for prosthetic-valve endocarditis within 12 months of surgery?
items.exp: '· < 12 months : CoNS > mRSA > Gram -ve bacilli'. (Book p1048)

items.q: What mortality figure is printed for acute infective endocarditis?
Acute IE — match — 1) Associated conditions 2) Valve consequence 3) Management … A) Destroyed valves B) Management of sepsis C) Abscess, osteomyelitis → severe sepsis, septic shock (MRSA)
items.exp: 'Associated condition : Abscess, osteomyelitis → Severe sepsis, Septic shock (mRSA)'; 'Destroyed valves'; 'management : of Sepsis'. (Book p1048)

items.q: A patient with acute IE, multiple abscesses and MRSA bacteraemia deteriorates with shock. Which printed pair describes the complication and the management priority?
opts: Abscess/osteomyelitis with severe sepsis or septic shock — manage the sepsis
Immunological vasculitis with Osler nodes — give steroids
items.exp: The acute-IE block prints abscess and osteomyelitis leading to severe sepsis / septic shock with MRSA, and 'management : of Sepsis'. (Book p1048)
